title: EveryRoot: Learning Chess Moves and Search Allocation
description: EveryRoot investigates whether a chess engine can learn both which moves to play and how much search a position deserves. The architecture combines a Proximal Policy Optimization move policy with native alpha-beta search and a detached Soft Actor-Critic controller. The move policy learns from searched evaluations expressed as reinforcement-learning rewards, supplemented by imitation of search-selected moves. The controller learns search budgets and stopping decisions by balancing evaluation fidelity against computational cost. The aim is competitive chess strength with lower computational requirements, supporting an affordable chess-playing and analysis application. This report describes the architecture, the proposed contribution and the intended product. It presents research aims rather than established superiority over competing engines. The deposited package contains the architecture report and supporting documentation; engine source code and trained weights are excluded.
